## The question

Leaders at CU Boulder have reasonably asked what role a university has in a buffalo herd. Colorado's own examples suggest an answer: **a university does not need to own a herd to play an essential role in one.** CU could bring research, students, convening power, and long-term commitment.

## What CU could bring

::: {.cards}
[**Research** <br>Grassland, soil, water, fire, and climate science on a working landscape, with questions shaped together with Tribal partners.](why-cu.qmd#research){.card-link}

[**Teaching** <br>Field courses and student research for CU students and students from Tribal colleges, side by side.](why-cu.qmd#teaching){.card-link}

[**Partnerships on the land** <br>Working with cities, counties, and federal land managers that already manage open space and herds.](why-cu.qmd#land){.card-link}

[**Relationships with Tribal Nations** <br>A lasting commitment that goes beyond statements, built around a goal many Tribal Nations are already pursuing: returning buffalo to the land.](why-cu.qmd#relationships){.card-link}
:::

## How a partnership could work

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  T["Tribal Nations<br/>cultural direction, priorities,<br/>where buffalo go"]
  L["Land partners<br/>city, county, or<br/>federal open space"]
  C["CU Boulder<br/>research, students,<br/>convening, data"]
  H(["A herd and the land it lives on"])
  T --> H
  L --> H
  C --> H
```

Three versions of this, from lightest to most involved, are laid out on [Partnership models](partnership.qmd). In every version, CU's part would be shaped with Tribal Nations from the start, and existing partners such as the InterTribal Buffalo Council would have a place at the table.

## A first step

The lightest first step is a **planning year**: CU convenes Tribal Nations, the people who already run Colorado's herds, and interested faculty, and listens before proposing anything. [A first step](next-steps.qmd) describes what that year could include.
